etymology: from Medieval Latin supersedere 'to sit above, refrain', from super- 'over' + sedere 'to sit'.

similar.description: spelled with 'sede', not 'cede' (unlike precede).

memory_tip: super(上)+sed(坐)→取而代之，注意 sede 拼写。

examples: The superstructure of the bridge was built.
A superstructure rose above the hull.
etymology: from super- 'above' + structure (Latin structura 'a building').

similar.description: superstructure is the part built above the base.

memory_tip: super(上)+structure(结构)→上层建筑。

etymology: from supplement + -ary; supplement from Latin supplere 'to fill up' (sub- + plere 'to fill').

similar.description: supplement is noun/verb; supplementary the adjective.

memory_tip: sup(下/补)+ple(满,如complete)+mentary→补充的。

etymology: from supposed (past of suppose) + -ly; suppose from Latin supponere 'to place under'.

similar.description: suppose is the verb; supposedly the adverb.

memory_tip: suppose(假定)+dly→据说，据称。

etymology: from Latin suppositionem 'a placing under' (sub- + ponere 'to place') + -ion.

similar.description: suppose is the verb; supposition the noun.

memory_tip: sub(下)+posit(放)+ion→推测，假定。

examples: A surcharge applied to late payments.
etymology: from French surcharge (sur- 'over' + charge 'load'); an extra charge.

similar.description: charge is the base fee; surcharge is added on top.

memory_tip: sur(上)+charge(费)→附加费，加收。

examples: The peak was surmounted at dawn.
etymology: from Old French surmonter (sur- 'over' + monter 'to mount'); to overcome.

similar.description: mount is to climb; surmount is to get over.

memory_tip: sur(上)+mount(登)→克服，越过。

examples: The movie kept us in suspense.
etymology: from Latin suspensus 'hung up, doubtful' (suspendere 'to hang'); anxious uncertainty.

similar.description: suspend is the verb; suspense the noun state.

memory_tip: sus(上)+pens(挂,如pendulum)→悬疑，焦虑。

examples: The suspension of the service angered users.
Suspension of the player was announced.
etymology: from Latin suspensionem 'a hanging up' (suspendere 'to hang') + -ion.

similar.description: suspend is the verb; suspension the noun.

memory_tip: sus(上)+pens(挂)+ion→暂停/悬挂，悬浮。

examples: They sought sustenance in the wild.
etymology: from Old French sustenance, from Latin sustinere 'to uphold' (sub- + tenere 'to hold').

similar.description: sustain is the verb; sustenance the noun (food/support).

memory_tip: sus(下)+ten(持,如tennis)+ance→营养/生计，记‘维持之物’。

examples: The car swerved to avoid the dog.
etymology: from Old English sweorfan 'to file, rub away'; later to turn aside.

similar.description: do not confuse with 'serve' or 'curve'.

memory_tip: 古英语‘擦/偏’→swerve，突然转向。

etymology: from 16th c., perhaps from Dutch zwirlen 'to whirl'; imitative.

similar.description: whirl is faster spin; swirl a gentler spiral.

memory_tip: 荷兰语‘旋’→swirl，打旋，漩涡。

etymology: from Greek sullabē 'a taking together' (sun- 'with' + lambanein 'to take').

similar.description: syllabus is a course outline; syllable a unit of sound.

memory_tip: 希腊‘一起拿取’→音节，记‘拼合之音’。

etymology: from New Latin syllabus, misprint of Greek sittybos 'a label/parchment'.

similar.description: syllable is sound unit; syllabus is the course plan.

memory_tip: 新拉丁‘课程提纲’→教学大纲，别与syllable混。

etymology: from symbol + -ize; symbol from Greek symbolon 'a sign, token' (sun- 'together' + ballein 'to throw').

similar.description: symbol is the sign; symbolize the verb.

memory_tip: sym(共同)+bol(抛,如ball)+ize→象征，记‘共同标记’。

examples: Find a synonym for the word.
etymology: from Latin synonymum, from Greek synōnumon (sun- 'together' + onoma 'name').

similar.description: antonym is opposite; synonym is same meaning.

memory_tip: syn(同)+onym(名,如name)→同义词，记‘同名’。

examples: He wrote a synopsis of the book.
etymology: from Greek sunopsis 'a seeing together' (sun- 'with' + opsis 'sight').

similar.description: share ops- 'sight'; synopsis is a summary.

memory_tip: syn(一起)+opsis(看)→概要，记‘综览’。

etymology: from synthesis + -ize; synthesis from Greek sunthesis 'a putting together' (sun- + tithenai 'to place').

similar.description: synthesis is the noun; synthesize the verb.

memory_tip: syn(一起)+thes(放,如thesis)+ize→合成，综合。

etymology: from Latin tacitus 'silent, unspoken' (tacere 'to be silent') + -it.

similar.description: taciturn means disinclined to speak; tacit means unspoken.

memory_tip: 拉丁‘沉默’→心照不宣的，默许的。

examples: Take the book from the shelf.
etymology: from Old Norse taka 'to grasp, take'; replaced Old English niman.

similar.description: took is the past of take (irregular).

memory_tip: 古诺斯语‘拿’→take，过去式 took 不规则。
